label: Model estimates
method: Return = weekly half-PPR points minus a pre-game line. The line is the pipeline projection from earlier weeks only (current-team average times the shrunk defense factor). Quarterbacks also add their earlier passing-touchdown and interception rates, because the yardage model does not project those. A trailing average is used when that projection is missing. A quarterback is not correlated with himself, so that cell stays blank. Players under 4 scored games are omitted. Each metric shrinks toward the position mean with a prior of 4 games. A good or bad script is the team's points versus its own earlier scoring average, not a sportsbook total.

tooltips.meanExcess: Mean excess: how many half-PPR points he has finished above the pre-game line, on average.
tooltips.volatility: Volatility: how wide those week-to-week finishes swing around that line.
tooltips.sharpe: Sharpe: steady over-the-line production per unit of week-to-week swing.
tooltips.upsideCapture: Upside capture: in weeks the offense scores above its usual total, how much of that good script shows up in his surplus.
tooltips.downsideCapture: Downside capture: in weeks the offense scores under its usual total, how far his surplus falls with that quiet script.
tooltips.beta: Beta: how tightly his half-PPR points move with the points his team scores.
tooltips.skew: Skew: whether his misses are mostly quiet weeks or the occasional huge week.
tooltips.tailRate: Tail rate: share of games he at least doubled the pre-game line.
tooltips.qbCorrelation: QB correlation: whether his big weeks land in the same games as his quarterback's.
